To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the increase of the local stock of low skilled immigrants has a positive effect on the profits and a negative effect on the labour costs of firms operating in the same local labour market.

the increase in low skill immigration that has taken place in Italy over the last 10 to 15 years has had a negative impact on productivity growth in local labour markets, and has reduced the growth of average wages.

a) low skilled immigration increases profits, but has no effect on productivity; b) the effect on profits is stronger for small firms operating low tech sectors and in areas specializing in the production of low skill goods; c) the effects of immigration on profits and productivity are stronger for firms with a higher share of unskilled workers in the labour force.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of immigration on firms and their performance.
the effects of immigration on the performance and productivity of local firms.
the effect that immigration may have on the economic performance of firms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of low-skilled immigration on the performance and productivity of Italian firms are positive but limited.
immigration is not bad for the economy, but it is not necessarily good either.
the effect of the immigration on the Italian economy is not positive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of immigration on the local economy are positive and significant, but small.
low skill immigration is not a panacea for the problems of the low tech manufacturing sectors.
low skilled immigration has not been beneficial to Italian manufacturing firms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
immigration policies should not be designed only with an eye on the labour market, but should take into account the effects on firm performance.
the economic impact of immigration is likely to vary substantially across sectors and across firms.

the effects of low skilled immigration on the economy are not necessarily neutral and that they depend on the specific features of the host country and on the specific characteristics of the immigrant population.
